method: Verified actual bytes of every one of the 193 assigned deployment/tooling files against frozen full6 and the full5 reviewed semantic baseline. Fully reread the two changed files and the unchanged production releasePreflight/checkBuild implementation, traced the real validator call and retained integration assertions, and verified original failed-matrix artifacts and subsequent exact-case targeted results. The 191 unchanged files use the prior complete semantic review plus current consumer-impact review, not a claim of newly rereading every unchanged body or reusing the old digest as current audit evidence. No test suite was executed during this audit.

baseline.coverage: The same complete 146-file deployment and 47-file tooling/workflow/test scope; no added, removed or omitted scope files.

semanticReview: The artifact test still constructs the real isolated Git fixture, commits the source-bound authorization, and invokes the complete releasePreflight(build:true) once. Its source digest/count and pins are taken from that actual result.

The three mutations still invoke production checkBuild directly: altered output bytes, an additional artifact, and a missing required runtime output. All three original refusal expectations remain. There is no validation mock or precomputed successful artifact inventory.

Production releasePreflight still invokes that same checkBuild after exact committed-source, authorization, pins, and real push/PR plan validation, then rechecks source and authorization. No production script changed in this repair.

Separate tests retain complete preflight/reuse/evidence-only-commit behavior, failed rebuild record removal, and source mutation during build. Exact head, checksum, committed authorization, raw Git bytes/executable bits, untracked source, workflow pins/triggers, release full selection, baseline ancestry and CLI option rejection remain checked.

The shared 15000 ms test timeout, 15000 ms hook timeout and four-worker configuration match the frozen full5 source. No sleep, retry, timeout increase, lower concurrency, case removal or new platform skip was introduced.

The maintainer lesson accurately distinguishes local full-matrix failures from hosted Reviewed checks, real first-selection behavior from stale expectations, and safe consumer/readiness assertions from weakening the implementation. It preserves re-audit and authorization requirements after source changes.

The unchanged deployment publication, cache/ownership, bounded JSON, receipt/recovery, process cleanup, history-copy, HTTPS and workspace contracts have no new runtime caller or persisted-format change from the two in-scope edits. The provider UI state repair is independently reviewed in the web scope; this report does not substitute for that review.

observations: Windows six failures and Linux five failures reconcile to seven distinct assertions in six files; four assertions failed on both platforms. A pass on the other platform does not erase a failure.

The failed JavaScript groups omit case arrays in aggregate reports; original raw Vitest JSON remains the per-assertion authority, with platform skips recorded rather than reported as zero coverage gaps.
Root 355 passes, ordinary Python Windows 540 passes/112 skips and Linux 651 passes/one skip, and each platform Go 20 passes remain separate from the failed JavaScript groups.
The old full5 audit digest and candidate remain historical evidence only. The repaired snapshot has a new full6 digest and does not inherit a successful full matrix.

The first-provider probe is labeled an additional reproduction, not another matrix case. The timeout diagnosis records missing CPU/I/O profiling and does not assert an unobserved precise host-load cause.

windows.skip: tests/tooling/ci-checks.test.ts::root fixtures have a traversable disposable temp outside their private home

targetedEvidenceReview.review: Rehashed all nine declared targeted/source artifacts, read both raw Vitest reports, verified exact identical 62-case ID sets and the unchanged Windows platform-only skip passing on Linux. These are prior narrow repair checks, not tests newly executed by full6 audit or proof of matrix timing under arbitrary load.

limitations: No full suite, additional targeted suite, production/service operation, external provider/MCP call, GitHub request, commit or deployment was performed during this audit.

The fixture build commands intentionally use small offline executable stand-ins to test preflight orchestration; they are not a substitute for actual candidate TypeScript/Vite builds or the full matrix.
No artificial contention profile was run; the targeted three-second artifact case does not guarantee a full-matrix timing outcome.
Actual clean full6 scope review is separate from the parent aggregate clean gate. A new exact-source authorization and complete matrix remain required before publishing.
Five delegated root fixture files and three Go entry/lock files remain in the root reviewer scope; this report claims exactly its assigned 193 files.
